children: Exxonmobil Holdings Corporation (NYSE:XOM) reported strong Q2 cash flows and record Permian output while facing operational hiccups — a Guyana FPSO fire probe and a missed White House refinery meeting — even as XTO redeems 2036–2038 notes, Trump’s stake rose and the company completed a HQ move.
XOM Cash Flow Rise Driven By Permian
: XOM traded near $160–$168. Q2 operating cash flow $23.6B, free cash flow $17.2B, driven by record Permian output and integrated refining. Iranian exports fell to ~534k bpd in August.
: ExxonMobil (XOM) said XTO Energy will redeem all outstanding 2036–2038 senior notes on Sept 27, 2026, at 100% principal plus make-whole and accrued interest; payments via DTC or surrender to agent.
: Guyana regulators probe fire on ExxonMobil’s Liza Unity FPSO after operations paused; all crew safe, offloading finished and operations later resumed.
: Senate report shows Donald Trump’s ExxonMobil (XOM) stake rose ~32% since Jan 2, 2026. Estimated value revised from ~$3.18M–$12.45M (end‑2025) to ~$4.19M–$16.39M (Aug 17, 2026).
: ExxonMobil (XOM) was not invited to a White House meeting with oil executives on U.S. refining capacity and gasoline prices; other major refiners and independents attended, per White House.
: ExxonMobil (XOM) moved its headquarters from New Jersey after 144 years. Traders note the corporate relocation, which may affect tax, regulatory exposure and long‑term operational costs.
